question: Do ASv6.19's observed gains and regressions repeat under fresh calls, including the fixed difficult-note controls, or were the first paired differences incidental?
prompt_changes: None. Use the exact prompts already tested in contract-comparison-v1.

selection.rule: Union of all eight predeclared development-repeat note IDs and every note whose clean/not-clean result differs between the two versions in contract-comparison-v1. Preserve development source order. No final notes.
selection.why: This repeats all observed note-level gains and regressions, while retaining the original difficult-note controls rather than returning to only three familiar problem notes.

design.order: For each trial, visit the 12 input notes in source order. For trial 2, odd positions run ASv6.13 then ASv6.19 and even positions reverse that order. Trial 3 reverses trial 2's order at every position.
design.context: Each call uses a new isolated process/thread/workdir with one note, no tools, no web and no conversation history.
design.fixed: Sol low, binary, account, production runner, normalization, schema and exact source text. Concurrency one; one admitted job at a time with host pressure checks.

review: Review every subject and the complete source of every output. Apply the original plan and disclosed corrections identically across versions; preserve raw generations and all decisions.
interpretation: Compare all three outputs per selected note, including the first run. Report concrete mechanisms and all gains/regressions rather than selecting a favorable output.
If context/coverage gains repeat without persistent new fidelity errors, ASv6.19 may be a better working reference for the next controlled change, but remains unvalidated.
If gains disappear or regressions repeat, do not automatically retain ASv6.19; use the broader evidence to choose the next reference or isolate an instruction interaction.
Mixed results remain mixed. This selection cannot estimate corpus-wide accuracy or attribute an effect to one sentence.

Neither prompt passes its recorded first full-development run. These repeats are diagnostic and cannot erase those failures or authorize final validation. The fixed completion criteria remain unchanged.
